steps.text: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C). Grease an 8x4-inch loaf pan.
Stir together flour, baking powder, and salt in a large bowl. Stir in Cheddar until incorporated, then add milk and melted butter, and mix until a soft dough forms. Spoon dough into the prepared pan.
Bake in the preheated oven until a toothpick inserted in the center of the loaf comes out clean, about 35 to 40 minutes. Remove from the pan and let cool.

raw_recipe.headline: Cheese Loaf
raw_recipe.description: This easy cheese bread is made with mild Cheddar cheese. For a bigger impact, you can vary the flavor by using sharp or aged Cheddar, or even pepper Jack!
raw_recipe.name: Cheese Loaf

review.reviewBody: *****EDIT***** I really like this bread, and because it is so easy I have done several things with it. This time, I had some Pepper Jack cheese and mozzarella that needed to be used. Excellent, as always. I like that this bread is quick, delicious and doesn't need any other ingredients than what I have at hand. I made a few minor changes, using Olive oil instead of butter and switching a half cup of flour for a half cup of wheat germ. These aren't necessary, but are dietary preferences. For additional flavor I added about a tablespoon of Italian seasoning to the dough. The dough is not what I would call soft, but stiff based on my experience. I had to pat it into the pan (I used a glass brownie pan) but it looks and smells wonderful. This is one I use again. Thank you.

Made a few changes, used strong bread flour and yeast also added tbsp of dried oregano. Result very pleasing and will make again. However I found that it did need slightly longer baking time than in your recipe. Very good though, many thanks. Just one thing though, to save time could you also have the metric equivalents on your recipes, this side of the pond sadly we have forsaken the old imperial measures. Thanks.

I will definitely make this again! I did add to the recipe and it is fantastic. I increased the amount of the cheese, the milk to 2 cups, used garlic salt at 1 1/2 teaspoons rather than regular salt, added 1 1/2 teaspoons of parsley, and 1 chopped jalapeño. I made two loafs, one with jalapeños and one with out. I also made mini muffins from the left over dough.

Have had this recipe for years and make it at least twice a week. Must say I changed the milk to buttermilk as well as added a scant 1/4 tsp. of baking soda to the dry ingredients to accommodate the buttermilk, as we prefer quick breads made with buttermilk rather than milk. 

I also add a good handful of chopped chives every now and then when available in my garden.

This is very good! I was concerned with the comments that the dough was very dry. Was not confident when my dough was still very dry after adding all the milk. Didnt work the dough too much and added it to the pan with dry lumps. Guess the cheese added the extra moisture as the result was lovely soft biscuit bread with a crunchy crust. Followed recipe except to use 1 c milk abd 1/2 c cream. Will definitely make again.

I did not have beer to make my usual beer bread, and we were having an Italian dinner... Must have bread! I went searching and found this recipe. I found the dough to be pretty dry, so I added a little extra milk and butter. I increased the amount of cheese, as well. The results were AMAZING!! The bread is very hearty. Next time, I would like to try putting herbs in it.

I liked the way it turned out. It wasn't dry or to moist it came out just right. I didn't change anything, but I did add to the recipe. I added chopped garlic and Italian seasonings to it. I will be making this again because the recipe is so versatile, so cheers to the creator of this recipe. Thank you.

This bread was really nice, but more like a tea biscuit loaf, I think. I will make it again with a stronger cheese if I can... it was just lacking a little flavour. I used Old cheese. It was great with strawberry jam.
3 minutes to mixing, 35 minutes to bake, cool cut eat. I thought my breadmaker was great but this is a keeper. I added a little bit more cheese.
I used Sharp white cheddar and medium cheddar. I also added fresh thyme. This bread recipe has lots of options! We really enjoyed it with fresh mushroom soup.
Made as muffins; 350 degrees for 20 minutes.

I didn’t know that cheese loaf was a real thing. I looked it up curious what would pop up and this did. It is very delicious, highly recommended. It saved me from Pete on 2 different occasions. A wise man once said Cheese loaf is what made us the great nation we are today. Sincerely,
Could use a bit more salt. I baked it in a stone loaf pan it could have used about 5 more minutes of baking time.
I made biscuits using this recipes and it makes about 15 and cooks for about 20-25 minutes. They are delicious!
This bread was great!! So good with sausage for breakfast, the only changes was I used 2cups of mild cheddar, 1/2 cup of mix white cheeses, and added dry herbs for some flavor. Was amazing!!
Thought it was a heavy bread without much taste. I won't make again unless it tastes better toasted.

I followed instructions, no substitutions but I did add a bit of jarred garlic for some extra flavoring but it was still pretty bland. I did enjoy it with butter spread on each slice though. I was very good that way. If it had more of a flavor to it i'd have given it 5 stars, couldn't have been any easier to make. No yeast or egg needed.. which is nice! :)
Created a gorgeous crisp crust. Was super simple. Definately going to have to make again.
